chunks: And by this chain, from Marwak ibn 'Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Tabari, who said:
I was standing by the head of al-Rida عليه السلام in Khurasan, and with him were a number of the Banu Hashim, among whom was Ishaq ibn Musa ibn 'Isa al-'Abbasi.

So he said: O Ishaq, it has reached me that the people are saying that we claim that the people are our slaves. No, by my kinship to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I have never said it at all, nor did I hear any of my forefathers say it, nor has it reached me from any of my forefathers that he said it.
But I do say: the people are devoted to us in obedience, and loyal to us in the religion. So let the one who is present convey it to the one who is absent.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Rida, the Imam speaking in this report
key_terms.عَبِيدٌ لَنَا: servants/slaves to us; here denied in the literal sense attributed by others
key_terms.فَلْيُبَلِّغِ الشَّاهِدُ الْغَائِبَ: let the present convey to the absent; an instruction to transmit the teaching accurately
key_terms.فِي الدِّينِ: in the religion; specifying the religious context of that loyalty
key_terms.فِي الطَّاعَةِ: in obedience; indicating the sphere in which allegiance to the Imams applies
key_terms.مَوَالٍ لَنَا: loyal to us; meaning those bound to the Imams through religious devotion and wilayah

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Rida عليه السلام say that people are slaves of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam al-Rida عليه السلام rejecting the false claim that the Ahl al-Bayt assert literal ownership of people as slaves. He clarifies instead that their rightful station is one of obedience and religious loyalty, affirming the authority of the Imams عليه السلام in the religion. The report also emphasizes accurate transmission of their teachings and the rejection of distorted attributions.

en.hubeali: And by this chain, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Muhammad Bin Zayd Al Tabary who said,

‘I was standing by the head of Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> at Khurasan, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence were a number from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>, and among them was Is’haq Bin Musa Bin Isa Al-Abbasy.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Is’haq! It has reached me<sup>asws</sup> that the people are saying that we<sup>asws</sup> are claiming that the people are our<sup>asws</sup> slaves. No! By my<sup>asws</sup> relationship from Rasool-Alah<sup>saww</sup>! I<sup>asws</sup> did not say it at all, nor had I<sup>asws</sup> heard it from my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> saying it, nor has it reached me from anyone from my<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said it.

But, I<sup>asws</sup> am saying, the people are slaves of ours<sup>asws</sup> regarding the obedience, friends of ours<sup>asws</sup> in the Religion. So let the attendees deliver it to the absentees’.
en.sarwar: 10. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Marwak ibn ‘Ubayd from Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Tabari who has said the following.
“I was in the presence of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) in Khurasan with a group of Hashimite people among them was Issshaq ibn Musa ibn ‘Isa from Abbasides

and the Imam (a.s.) said to Ishaq, “I hear that people say we think they are our slaves. I swear upon my close relation with the holy Prophet (s.a.) that I have never said such a thing nor Have I ever heard any such thing from my father and grandfather nor I have received any such report from my (holy and noble) ancestors who may have said any such thing.
But I must say that people are our slaves in the matters of obedience to us. They are our friends in religion. Those present here must tell this to those who are not present here.”
